"""Component layers.0.mlp.down_proj:3073: a "doubled logical operator" detector.

What it does: this direction of the layer-0 MLP output is pushed strongly negative
when the current token is a doubled logical or bar operator, `&&` or `||` (as in C,
Java, JavaScript, Rust, shell or wiki tables), by about -6.5. It is weakly negative on
a few other operator symbols (`<<`, `::`, `=>`, `===`, `##`) and on a few words
about lines and suppositions ("parallel", "perpendicular", "adjacent", "suppose").
On every other token it is close to 0.

Why: the token's own identity is all this program reads; the component has no
context dependence worth modelling for a short description.
"""

READS = ()

# Doubled logical / bar operators: strong negative response.
LOGIC_VALUE = -6.5

# Weaker negative responses to some other operator symbols and words.
TOKEN_VALUES = {
    "<<": -1.1,
    "::": -0.5,
    "=>": -0.5,
    "===": -0.5,
    "##": -0.5,
    "parallel": -3.5,
    "perpendicular": -1.5,
    "adjacent": -1.0,
    "supposed": -1.9,
    "suppose": -1.0,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = tok.strip()
    if "&&" in tok or "||" in tok:
        return carry, LOGIC_VALUE
    return carry, float(TOKEN_VALUES.get(word, 0.0))

programs.sol:
"""Negative responses to familiar action/direction compound words.

The largest responses are to setup, layout and hookup; other listed compounds
(e.g. lookup, login, backup) have progressively weaker responses. Matching
ignores outer identifier punctuation and ordinary capitalization. Most plurals
are weaker. A few Chinese/Japanese equivalents are included. The phrase
'set up' is recognized from the preceding token, resetting at document changes.
Unlisted words receive zero: this deliberately omits weaker lexical preferences
and most context-dependent and tokenization-dependent variation.
"""

READS = ()

# Familiar verb-particle nouns; levels approximate their observed response.
CONNECTIONS = set('setup layout hookup'.split())
SEARCH_AND_TRANSACTIONS = set(
    'checkout cleanup lookup payout pickup matchup'.split()
)
START_AND_ACCESS = set(
    'login startup signup popup playback'.split()
)
ACTION_COMPOUNDS = set('''
backup lineup makeup breakup buildup meetup roundup wakeup
rollout workout turnout knockout
breakout bailout fallout shootout dropout logout teardown shutdown slowdown
lockdown meltdown rundown showdown cutoff payoff kickoff takeover crossover
leftover feedback fallback comeback markup uptake getaway breakdown
'''.split())
FLOW_AND_RESULTS = set('''
workflow overlap overlay outcome outbreak intake backend frontend dropdown
'''.split())


def response(word):
    plural = word.endswith('s')
    stem = word[:-1] if plural else word
    if stem in CONNECTIONS:
        return -3.8
    if stem in SEARCH_AND_TRANSACTIONS:
        value = -2.8
    elif stem in START_AND_ACCESS:
        value = -2.1
    elif stem in ACTION_COMPOUNDS:
        value = -1.4
    elif stem in FLOW_AND_RESULTS:
        value = -0.85
    elif stem in {'timeout', 'usage', 'delivery'}:
        value = -0.9
    elif stem in {'callback', 'breakthrough', 'walkthrough', 'setback',
                   'rollback', 'giveaway', 'takeaway'}:
        value = -0.6
    elif stem in {'turnover', 'makeover', 'lookout', 'standout',
                   'blackout', 'countdown', 'cooldown', 'runoff'}:
        value = -0.8
    elif stem == '布局':  # Chinese: layout
        return -2.5
    elif stem in {'备份', '反馈', '登录', '退出', '流程', 'ダウン'}:
        # Backup, feedback, login, exit, workflow; Japanese 'down'.
        return -0.7
    else:
        return 0.0
    if plural and stem in {'outcome', 'outbreak'}:
        return -0.3
    return value * (0.75 if plural else 1.0)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    previous = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    word = raw.strip('_-./():').lower()
    value = response(word)
    if word == 'up' and previous in {'set', 'setting'}:
        value = -0.5
    # These camel-case method spellings receive weaker responses.
    spelling = raw.strip('_-./():')
    if spelling == 'setUp':
        value = -1.0
    elif spelling == 'SetUp':
        value = -1.8
    elif spelling in {'signUp', 'tearDown'}:
        value *= 0.5
    return (doc, word), value
programs.haiku:
"""Noun-ified phrasal verbs: one-word compounds made of a verb plus a particle
(setup, layout, login, checkout, lookup, cleanup, startup, signup, backup, popup,
shutdown, rollout, workout, breakdown, timeout, feedback, callback ...).
The component is pushed strongly negative on the last token of such a compound
(e.g. ' setup', ' layouts', ' checkout'), and is near zero on the verb or the particle
alone (' set', ' up', ' check', ' out'), and on almost all other text."""

import re

READS = ()

# Verbs that take a particle to make a compound noun (phrasal verbs).
VERBS = (
    "set", "lay", "look", "log", "sign", "check", "clean", "start", "back", "pop",
    "pick", "hook", "roll", "work", "pay", "wake", "match", "break", "shut", "lock",
    "drop", "bail", "knock", "shoot", "take", "cut", "slow", "build", "make", "line",
    "fall", "call", "feed", "time", "play", "tear", "turn", "melt", "cool", "count",
    "show", "run", "kick", "hand", "give", "crack", "step", "print",
)
# Particles that complete the compound.
PARTICLES = ("up", "down", "out", "back", "off", "over", "in", "away")

# Strongest, most typical UI/software compounds.
TOP = ("setup", "layout", "hookup", "checkout", "cleanup", "lookup", "signup",
       "pickup", "login", "startup", "backup", "popup")

COMPOUNDS = {v + p for v in VERBS for p in PARTICLES}


def _word(token):
    """The token as a bare lowercase word: no space, underscore, dot or 's' suffix."""
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z]", "", token.lower())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    w = _word(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    if w.endswith("s") and w[:-1] in COMPOUNDS:
        w = w[:-1]  # plural: layouts, workouts
    if w in TOP:
        return None, -3.0
    if w in COMPOUNDS:
        return None, -1.5
    return None, 0.0

"""Give a small negative pulse to selected compound-word patterns.

For the current token, this checks whether its ASCII letters split into two
listed word parts. It also recognizes “up” after “set”, “setting”, or “pop”
in the same document. These are only a readable approximation of the
component’s sparse lexical responses.
"""

READS = ()

PARTS = {
    "back", "down", "out", "in", "up", "off", "over", "under",
    "home", "page", "lock", "time", "front", "end", "work", "flow",
    "feed", "mark", "come", "take", "get", "line", "pop", "break",
    "lay", "wrap", "lap", "sub", "mission",
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    word = "".join(ch for ch in text if "a" <= ch <= "z")
    if not word:
        return None, 0.0

    same_document = (
        len(prefix) > 1
        and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    )
    previous = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() if same_document else ""
    phrasal_up = word == "up" and previous in {"set", "setting", "pop"}
    compound = phrasal_up or any(
        word[:cut] in PARTS and word[cut:] in PARTS
        for cut in range(2, len(word) - 1)
    )
    return None, -0.30 if compound else 0.0

programs.haiku:
"""Layer-0 MLP down-projection component 3076: an "S-word-start" detector.

What it does: it reads only the current token and predicts how strongly this component
writes into the residual stream there. It is high when the token's spelling begins with
the letter S, after any leading space or punctuation, so ' South', ' Saturday', 'sync',
'/src' and '-sc' all count. Capitalised and space-led words fire a little more than
lowercase or mid-word pieces. Tokens starting 'st' fire less, and possessive "'s" does not
fire. The digit 8 and the Cyrillic letter с (which sounds like s) fire at a similar level.
The chat tool-response tags '<tool_response>' and '</tool_response>' fire strongly. Every
other token predicts 0.

Why: its activation is mostly token identity (about 92% of variance is explained by a
per-token table). The table's top entries are S-initial words, which a short
spelling rule captures. What this simple version leaves out is the long tail of
token-specific values, which a full lookup table would add.
"""

READS = ()

LEADING = " \n\t\r"


def _word_start(token):
    # The first letter or digit of the token, skipping spaces and punctuation.
    for c in token.lstrip(LEADING):
        if c.isalnum():
            return c
    return ""


def activation(token):
    body = token.lstrip(LEADING)
    if body == "<tool_response>":
        return 3.0
    if body == "</tool_response>":
        return 1.0
    if body.startswith(("'", "’")):
        return 0.0  # possessive 's
    if body.strip() == "8":
        return 0.7
    first = _word_start(token)
    if first in ("с", "С"):  # Cyrillic es, sounds like s
        return 1.0
    if first not in ("s", "S"):
        return 0.0
    value = 1.0
    if first == "S":
        value += 0.3
    if token[:1] == " ":
        value += 0.1
    if body[:2].lower() == "st":
        value -= 0.4
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return None, float(activation(prefix.token_strings[-1]))

"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:3077 -- "code continuation after a capital letter".

The component is silent on almost all text. It responds only at a token that is
glued onto a preceding token ending in an upper-case letter, i.e. inside an
upper-case code, abbreviation or chemical formula (GS-09, AA-7, IL-1, Ag, Hg, Cd,
S-1, "Ti-Cu-Ag", "CD4", "AO", ...). There it has a sign that depends on what the
current token is:

  - a hyphen ("-")                -> positive (about +0.65): "GS-", "IL-", "S-1"
  - a digit                       -> positive (about +0.4):  "GS-0", "CD4", "RM2"
  - a colon                       -> weakly positive (+0.25)
  - a single lower-case letter    -> negative (about -0.7):  "Hg", "Ag", "Cb", "Yd"

Everywhere else (ordinary words, spaces, punctuation, the upper-case letter itself)
it predicts 0, which is its typical activation there.

The program keeps a one-token memory: it reads only the previous and current token.
"""

import re

READS = ()

HYPHENS = ("-", "‐")
CODE_END = re.compile(r"[A-Z]$")
SINGLE_LOWER = re.compile(r"_?[a-z]")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # Start of a document: nothing precedes the token.
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return None, 0.0
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()    # the token, ignoring a leading space
    if not CODE_END.search(prev):
        return None, 0.0
    if cur in HYPHENS:
        return None, 0.65
    if re.fullmatch(r"[0-9]", cur):
        return None, 0.4
    if cur == ":":
        return None, 0.25
    if SINGLE_LOWER.fullmatch(cur):
        return None, -0.7
    return None, 0.0

It goes strongly negative on the current token when that token is a form of the
verb/noun "express" (express, expressed, expression, expressions, expr, _expr, Expr),

"""

programs.sol:
"""Detect speaker-reference words, chiefly 'our' and its translations.

Spacing and capitalization distinguish whole-word-like tokens from fragments.
A decaying count of recent 'we' mentions weakens English 'our'; document starts
strengthen it. Unrecognized tokens get zero, omitting small unrelated responses.
"""

from math import exp, log1p, sqrt

READS = ()
DECAY = exp(-1 / 32)

# English forms: response with a leading space, then without one.
ENGLISH = {
    'our': (6.1, 2.0), 'Our': (6.6, 6.9), 'OUR': (5.0, 1.5),
    'ours': (2.3, 0.4), 'ourselves': (1.9, 0.0),
    'we': (1.3, 0.8), 'We': (1.25, 1.25), 'WE': (0.6, 0.4),
    'us': (1.6, 0.0), 'Us': (0.6, 0.2),
    'my': (0.9, 0.6), 'My': (0.5, 0.5), 'MY': (0.5, 0.2),
    'myself': (0.2, 0.0), 'its': (0.26, 0.0),
}

# Translations of 'our', including grammatical inflections and token stems.
POSSESSIVES = (
    (3.1, 'nuestro nuestra nuestros nuestras'),       # Spanish
    (3.9, 'nosso nossa nossos nossas noss'),         # Portuguese
    (3.3, 'nostro nostra nostri nostre'),            # Italian
    (3.7, 'notre unser unsere unserer unseren unserem unseres'),
    (3.5, 'наш наши нашей нашего наших'),             # Russian
    (4.6, 'нашем'),
    (1.3, 'nost'),
    (1.6, 'onze'),
    (2.4, '우리'),
)
POSSESSIVES = {word: value for value, words in POSSESSIVES
               for word in words.split()}

# Plural speaker pronouns, and common verbs explicitly meaning 'we have'.
SPEAKERS = {
    'nous': 1.0, 'Nous': 1.0, 'nos': 0.7, 'Notre': 1.1,
    'wir': 1.0, 'Wir': 0.9, 'uns': 0.4,
    'мы': 0.7, 'Мы': 1.0, 'нас': 0.9, 'нам': 0.8,
    'noi': 0.9, 'nosotros': 1.3, 'ons': 1.2, 'wij': 0.3,
    'kita': 0.9, 'kami': 0.9,
    'avons': 1.0, 'abbiamo': 1.2, 'hemos': 1.0,
}


def word_value(token):
    word = token.strip()
    spaced = token.startswith(' ')
    if word in ENGLISH:
        return ENGLISH[word][not spaced]
    if word[:1] in ('"', '“', '.'):
        if word[1:] == 'Our':
            return 4.4
        if word[1:] == 'We':
            return 1.4
    if spaced:
        return POSSESSIVES.get(word, SPEAKERS.get(word, 0.0))
    if word in ('Nous', 'Wir', 'Мы'):
        return 1.0
    for we in ('我们', '我們'):
        if we in word:
            if word == we + '的':
                return 4.6
            if word == we:
                return 2.6
            if word.startswith(('让', '讓')) or word.endswith('将'):
                return 1.4
            return 2.0
    if word in ('咱们', '咱們'):
        return 1.7
    if word in ('我々', '私たち'):
        return 2.0
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != document:
        position, recent_we = 0, 0.0
    else:
        _, position, recent_we = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = word_value(token)
    if token in (' our', ' Our', 'Our'):
        capitalized = token.strip() == 'Our'
        base = 6.5 if capitalized else 6.25
        boost = (3.2 if token.startswith(' ') else 4.5) if capitalized else 2.3
        penalty = 1.1 if capitalized else 1.4
        value = base + boost / sqrt(position + 1) - penalty * log1p(recent_we)
    recent_we = DECAY * recent_we + (token in (' we', ' We', 'We', 'we'))
    return (document, position + 1, recent_we), value

programs.haiku:
"""Layer-0 MLP down-projection component 3080 (Qwen3-1.7B).

What it does, in plain terms: a token-level detector. It is silent on most text (numbers
and punctuation barely move it) and fires on a few families of short word pieces:
  1. "ex"-type pieces, the strongest trigger: " ex", "ex", "Ex", " EX", "_EX", "\tex",
     "px", "Tx", "rx", "ox" (about 0.6 to 0.8 when they occur);
  2. a bare letter x or X as a piece, also "(x", "/x", "\\x", " X" (about 0.2 to 0.4);
  3. test-result check marks and PASS markers ("✓", " PASS") (about 0.4);
  4. a handful of tech / product-name pieces ("Act", "Pro", "mod", "micro", "match")
     (about 0.3).
Everywhere else it predicts 0. The values are the mean activations measured on sample
text, rounded. The program is a simple lookup on the current token only; it ignores
context and carries no state.

  - "do" as a syllable in other writing systems (ド, ど, 도, до, 多, 做, โดน): medium.
  - other words that begin with "do" (doctor, domain, dose, docs, ...): weak.
  - words that merely contain "do" in the middle (todo, undo, ado): very weak.
Everything else predicts 0. Stateless: each position is judged from its own token.

Main program: `predict` below is the whole explanation; `step` is the contract form.
"""

READS = ()

# Spelled-out forms of "do" -> how strongly the component responds.
DO_WORDS = {
    "do": 3.0,
    "does": 1.7,
    "doing": 1.5,
    "did": 1.4,
    "done": 1.0,
    "don": 1.0,
    "doesn": 0.5,
    "didn": 0.6,
    "dont": 0.6,
    "doesnt": 0.6,
}
# The "t" of a negated do-form: "don't", "didn't", "doesn't".
NEGATION_STEMS = {"don", "didn", "doesn", "dont"}
# The syllable "do" written in other scripts (katakana ド, hiragana ど, Hangul 도, Cyrillic до,
# Chinese 多 / 做 / 道 pronounced in similar ways, Thai โดน).
OTHER_SCRIPT_DO = {"ド", "ど", "도", "до", "多", "做", "道", "โดน"}
# Words beginning with "do" that are not the verb-like "do" family.
NOT_DO_WORDS = {
    "down", "double", "download", "downloads", "downloaded", "downtown", "downstream",
    "downward", "document", "dollars", "doubled", "doubles", "doubtful", "dog", "dogs",
    "door", "dot", "dove", "dozen", "dough", "doll",
}


def _word(token: str) -> str:
    return token.strip().lower().replace("’", "'")


def activation(token: str, previous: str) -> float:
    """Predicted activation for one token, given the token before it."""
    word = _word(token)
    if word in DO_WORDS:
        return DO_WORDS[word]
    if word == "'t" and _word(previous) in NEGATION_STEMS:
        return 0.8
    if word in OTHER_SCRIPT_DO:
        return 1.3
    if word.startswith("do") and word not in NOT_DO_WORDS:
        return 0.4
    if "do" in word:
        return 0.2
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    previous = tokens[-2] if len(tokens) > 1 else ""
    return None, float(activation(tokens[-1], previous))

"""Detect short written e-vowel syllables, especially Japanese katakana.

Numbers are average responses fitted on training text. Columns distinguish
hiragana, katakana, and a katakana completed by a separate UTF-8 byte token.
Longer tokens dilute the syllable response; small kana change the vowel of
the preceding kana. Korean and Thai e-syllables are recognized separately.
Other katakana get a small negative baseline; most other text gets zero.
This approximates the strong responses, not the weaker lexical variation.
"""
import unicodedata

READS = ()

#                hiragana  katakana  split katakana
E_SYLLABLES = {
    'え': (-.65, -2.5, -5.2),
    'け': (-1.2, -4.7, -5.0),
    'げ': (-1.7, -3.5, -4.1),
    'せ': (-2.3, -3.2, -5.5),
    'ぜ': (-1.0, -3.5, -3.3),
    'て': (-.35, -4.55, -6.3),
    'で': (-1.2, -3.8, -7.9),
    'ね': (-1.9, -2.9, -4.1),
    'へ': (-.55, -2.4, -2.8),
    'べ': (-2.65, -4.9, -4.3),
    'ぺ': (-2.2, -2.85, -4.2),
    'め': (-3.4, -4.4, -5.0),
    'れ': (-1.65, -4.5, -4.9),
}


def kana_response(text, split):
    value, length = 0.0, 0.0
    for i, c in enumerate(text):
        if c == 'ー':
            length += .5
            continue
        if c in 'ァィゥェォャュョぁぃぅぇぉゃゅょ':
            continue  # Count these with the preceding kana.
        katakana = 'ァ' <= c <= 'ヺ'
        hira = chr(ord(c) - 96) if katakana else c
        small = text[i + 1:i + 2]
        if small and small in 'ェぇ':
            score = -2.6  # An e-vowel digraph, such as フェ or シェ.
        elif small and small in 'ァィゥォャュョぁぃぅぉゃゅょ':
            score = -.2  # ディ, for example, is di rather than de.
        elif hira in E_SYLLABLES:
            column = 2 if split and katakana else int(katakana)
            score = E_SYLLABLES[hira][column]
        else:
            score = -.2 if katakana else 0.0
        value += score
        if c.isalpha():
            length += 1
    if text in ('ェ', 'ぇ'):
        return -2.6
    return value / max(1.0, length) ** 1.7


def korean_response(c, split):
    code = ord(c) - 0xac00
    onset, vowel, final = code // 588, code // 28 % 21, code % 28
    if vowel == 5:  # ㅔ
        value = -2.6
        if onset == 6:  # m
            value = -3.9
        elif onset == 3:  # d
            value = -6.7 if split else -3.1
        elif onset == 16:  # t
            value = -5.3 if split else -3.9
        elif onset in (1, 12, 13):  # tense k, j, tense j
            value = 0.0
        elif onset == 9:  # s
            value = -.5
        elif onset in (14, 18):  # ch, h
            value = -.8
        if final:
            value *= .2
    elif vowel == 1:  # ㅐ: strongest with sonorant or labial onsets.
        value = -1.1 if onset in (2, 5, 6, 11) else 0.0
        if onset in (7, 17):
            value = -1.3
        if final:
            value *= .2
    elif vowel == 15:  # ㅞ
        value = -1.5 if not final else -.3
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    split = '\ufffd' in text
    if split:
        same_document = (prefix.position > 0 and
                         prefix.document_ids[-1] == prefix.document_ids[-2])
        whole = prefix.text_prefixes[-1] if same_document else text
        if whole and whole[-1] != '\ufffd':
            text = whole[-1]
        else:
            # Some tokens contain a visible vowel and an unfinished next letter.
            if 'े' in text:
                return None, -3.0
            text = text.replace('\ufffd', '')
            split = False

    # Halfwidth kana are the same syllables, with a weaker response.
    halfwidth = any('ｦ' <= c <= 'ﾟ' for c in text)
    if halfwidth:
        text = unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', text)

    if any('ぁ' <= c <= 'ヺ' for c in text):
        value = kana_response(text, split)
        if halfwidth:
            value *= .7
    elif len(text) == 1 and '\uac00' <= text <= '\ud7a3':
        value = korean_response(text, split)
    elif text.startswith('เ'):
        # Thai's written e precedes its consonant. Closed/longer tokens are weaker.
        value = -2.8 / max(1, len(text) - 1) ** 2.1
        if len(text) == 2:
            if text[1] in 'กทลด':
                value = -3.6
            elif text[1] in 'ขหต':
                value = -1.7
    elif text in ('ε', 'έ', 'Ε', 'Έ', 'э', 'Э'):
        value = -.5
    elif text == 'ে':  # Bengali e vowel sign.
        value = -4.0
    elif text == 'े':  # Devanagari e vowel sign.
        value = -.55
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return None, float(value)

"""Layer-0 MLP output component 3089 (layers.0.mlp.down_proj): the "e syllable" detector.

What it does: this component goes strongly negative on the current token when that token
is a syllable written in a non-Latin script whose vowel is /e/ (as in "ke", "te", "me",
"ge", "re"). The strongest case is a lone katakana e-syllable such as ケ, メ, デ, テ, レ, ベ
(about -4), then Hangul syllables with the vowel ㅔ and no final consonant (게, 메, 에; about
-2.8), Thai tokens built on the leading vowel sign เ (about -2.9), and lone hiragana
e-syllables such as め, せ, れ (about -1.3). Words containing an e-syllable are weaker. Other
katakana gets a small negative value, and Latin, Cyrillic, CJK and almost everything else is
zero, because the component is essentially a lookup of the current token's sound and script.

Why: the magnitudes were fitted by least squares to the component's activations on 512
training rows (variance explained about 0.40 in-sample for these groups). The rule only
reads the current token's own text, so it is stateless.
"""

import unicodedata

READS = ()

# The e-row of the kana syllabary: ke, se, te, ne, he, me, re, de, ze, ge, be, pe, and e.
KATAKANA_E = set("エェケセテネヘメレベペデゼゲヱヶ") | set("ｴｪｹｾﾃﾈﾍﾒﾚ")
HIRAGANA_E = set("えぇけせてねへめれべぺでげぜゑ")
GREEK_E = set("εέΕΈ")
THAI_E_SIGN = "เ"  # เ, the leading vowel sign for /e/


def _is_kana(ch):
    name = unicodedata.name(ch, "")
    return "KATAKANA" in name or "HIRAGANA" in name or ch in "ー・"


def _hangul_open_e(ch):
    # Hangul syllables are coded as (initial, vowel, final). Vowel 5 is ㅔ (/e/); final 0 means none.
    code = ord(ch) - 0xAC00
    return 0 <= code < 11172 and (code // 28) % 21 == 5 and code % 28 == 0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    if not text:
        return carry, 0.0
    if len(text) == 1:
        if text in KATAKANA_E:
            return carry, -4.0
        if text in HIRAGANA_E:
            return carry, -1.3
        if _hangul_open_e(text):
            return carry, -2.8
        if text in GREEK_E:
            return carry, -0.4
    if THAI_E_SIGN in text and len(text) <= 2:
        return carry, -2.9
    if all(_is_kana(ch) for ch in text) and any(ch in KATAKANA_E for ch in text):
        return carry, -0.6
    if any("KATAKANA" in unicodedata.name(ch, "") for ch in text):
        return carry, -0.25
    return carry, 0.0

What it does: this component adds a "maths and school subjects" signal to the
residual stream. It is near zero on nearly all text, and goes positive on the
words that name mathematics, a school or science subject, or a maths topic:
"Algebra", "Geometry", "trig", "calculus", "math", "matrix", "probability",
"worksheet", "coordinates", "quadratic", "determinant", "fractions", "factors",
and so on. Words split over several tokens (e.g. "Math" + "ematics") count
as whole words.

The strongest response is to the geometry sense of "Area" after a geometry
word, as in "Surface Area", "Total Area" or "Base Area" (about 1.6 activation
units). "Area" in other senses (e.g. "Government area") stays low.

The program reads each token's text, keeps the current word and the word before
it in its carry (reset at each document start), and scores the word. The weights
are in the component's activation units; they were set by hand from the measured
activations on training rows, and are not a fitted model.
"""

import re

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Names of a branch of maths, or a maths task or topic.
MATH_STRONG = re.compile(
    r"algebra|geometry|trig\w*|calcul(us|ator)|mathemat\w*|maths?"
    r"|worksheets?|homework|mensuration|probabilit\w*|matri(x|ces)"
    r"|determinant|quadratics?|discriminant|logarithm\w*|derivatives?"
    r"|integration|statistics|coordinates?|perimeter|centroid|fractions?"
    r"|permutations?",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
# Weaker maths and science words, common in maths text.
MATH_WEAK = re.compile(
    r"factors?|formula|graph|grade|percent\w*|exponent\w*|correlation"
    r"|inverse|sample|pyramids?|gmat|gre|vertex|equation|theorem"
    r"|polynomial|vectors?|proof|prove|linear|physics|chemistry|astronomy"
    r"|volume|surface|combinations?|binomial|deviation|college|biology"
    r"|economics|psychology|engineering|relativity",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
# Words that, just before "Area", make it the geometry sense.
GEOMETRY_BEFORE_AREA = {"surface", "total", "base", "lateral", "side"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (previous word, current word), or None at a row start.
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    prev, cur = carry if (carry is not None and not new_doc) else ("", "")
    if tok.strip().isalpha() and not tok[:1].isspace() and cur:
        cur += tok  # the word goes on: a token with no leading space
    elif tok.strip().isalpha():
        prev, cur = cur, tok.strip()  # a new word starts here
    else:

    if cur.lower() == "area":

    elif MATH_STRONG.fullmatch(cur):
        value = 0.3
    elif MATH_WEAK.fullmatch(cur):
        value = 0.2
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return (prev, cur), float(value)

  * the Latin letter x as a standalone symbol (x, X, (x, \\x, ' x', ...)  -> about 0.56
  * the "kh" sound in a token (Kh, Khan, akh, ikh, Sikh, ...)              -> about 1.5
  * the Cyrillic letter х and the Greek letter χ                          -> about 1.0
  * the Arabic letter خ (kha)                                             -> about 3.0
  * the Japanese kana ク / く / ウ (mid-word, used here as a rough k-sound) -> about 1.0

# Activation for a token containing the "kh" sound.
KH_SOUND = 1.5

ARABIC_KHA = 3.0

    return re.sub(r"[\W_]+", "", token).lower()

    return 0.0

    return carry, float(activation(prefix.token_strings[-1]))

only the newest token, and matches stems inside it. A stem must start a word, or start a
new word inside a camelCase name, and must not be followed by more lowercase letters, so
"table", "silicon" and "optional" do not match "tab", "icon" and "option".

    (5.7, ("button", "btn", "按钮", "钮", "кноп")),
    (2.9, ("checkbox",)),
    (1.4, ("menu", "option", "dropdown", "toolbar", "combo")),
    (1.0, ("label", "icon", "input", "item", "textfield", "textbox")),
    (0.5, ("click", "link", "tab", "arrow", "field", "panel")),

    camel = any(c.isupper() for c in word[1:]) and not word.startswith(('Mc', 'Mac'))
    if member or camel:
        value *= .15
    adverb_like = (word.endswith('ly') and word not in GIVEN
                   and word not in SURNAMES)
    if word.lower() in DISCOURSE or adverb_like:
        value = .10 if capital else .18
    return max(-3.0, min(.25, value))


# Initial letters differ in response, especially J and M; I is often a pronoun.
def initial_response(letter, strength):
    if letter == 'J':
        return -.30 - 1.30*strength
    if letter == 'M':
        return -.07 - .90*strength
    if letter == 'R':
        return -.03 - .80*strength
    if letter in 'IOQU':
        return .03 - .15*strength
    return .05 - .65*strength


BOUNDARIES = {
    ' and': (.03, -.51), ' &': (-.01, -.96), ' (': (.04, -.24),
    '.': (.006, -.08), ' ': (.012, -.11), ' Jr': (-.35, -.40),
    ' Sr': (-.20, -.40), ' MD': (-.40, -.65), ' II': (-.20, -.30),
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        text, last, saved = '', '', 0.0
    else:
        _, text, last, saved = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    initial = len(token) == 2 and token[0] == ' ' and token[1].isupper()
    joined = len(token) == 2 and token[0] in ',-' and token[1].isupper()
    active = (token in BOUNDARIES or initial or joined
              or token in (',', ' et', '.,', '.;'))
    value, next_saved = 0.0, 0.0
    if active:
        comma = name_boundary(text, last)
        strength = max(0.0, -comma)
        if text.endswith((',', ', ')):
            strength = max(strength, saved)
        if token == ',':
            value, next_saved = comma, strength
        elif initial:
            value = initial_response(token[1], strength)
        elif joined:
            value = -strength * (1.0 if token[0] == ',' else .65)
        elif token == ' et':
            words = WORDS.findall(text.rstrip(' ,'))
            capital = bool(words and words[-1][0].isupper())
            value = -.12 - .60*strength - 1.15*capital
            french = re.findall(
                r'\b(?:le|la|les|des|du|une|que|il|qui|dans|pour|avec|sur)\b',
                text.lower())
            if len(french) >= 2:
                value *= .15
        elif token in ('.,', '.;'):
            words = WORDS.findall(text)
            capital = bool(words and words[-1][0].isupper())
            value = -1.0 if text.endswith('et al') else (-1.1 if capital else -.03)
            next_saved = max(strength, -value)
        else:
            base, scale = BOUNDARIES[token]
            value = base + scale*strength
    elif token.isspace():
        next_saved = saved
    state = (doc, (text+token)[-180:], token, next_saved)
    return state, float(max(-3.0, value))

"""Layer-0 MLP feature 3134: a 'name-list punctuation' detector.

It goes negative on the small tokens that come right after a person's name in
citations and name lists:
  * the "et" of "Surname et al." (strongest after a capitalised surname),
  * the ".," after author initials ("M.D.,", "R.,"),
  * the "&" joining authors ("Taylor & Thompson"),
  * the comma after a name in a list of names (bibliographies, credits, lists of people).
The comma response grows with how name-like the recent text is (the share of capitalised
words or initials among the last 6 tokens of the document), and is stronger when the comma
follows a word fragment (the tail of a split, usually rare, surname such as "Voyn|ich,").
Everywhere else the feature is about zero, including on ordinary "however," style commas,
which are slightly positive.
"""

READS = ()
WINDOW = 6  # recent tokens used to judge how name-like the text is


def is_cap_word(s):
    # a token starting a capitalised word or an initial: " Smith", " J"
    return s[:1] == " " and s[1:2].isupper()


def is_fragment(s):
    # a token continuing a word begun by an earlier token (no leading space)
    return s[:1].isalpha()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    toks, docs, t = prefix.token_strings, prefix.document_ids, prefix.position
    cur = toks[t]
    recent = [i for i in range(max(0, t - WINDOW), t) if docs[i] == docs[t]]
    caps = sum(is_cap_word(toks[i]) for i in recent) / len(recent) if recent else 0.0
    has_prev = bool(recent) and recent[-1] == t - 1
    prev = toks[t - 1] if has_prev else ""
    if cur == " et":
        value = -0.65 - 0.6 * is_cap_word(prev)
    elif cur == ".,":
        value = -0.5
    elif cur == " &":
        value = -0.3
    elif cur == ",":
        frag = is_fragment(prev)
        value = -caps * (0.5 + 1.25 * frag) - 0.1 * frag
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, float(value)

"""Approximate an Italian-sensitive lexical response.

A leaky score counts Italian function words and characteristic spellings;
competing languages' function words subtract evidence. Word classes, productive
prefixes and spelling fragments then have a baseline plus an Italian-context
response. Prepositions and consonant clusters are usually positive; articles
and several endings are negative. The score resets between documents.
A separate rule handles the end-of-reasoning marker. All lexical rules use
word and spelling classes, not individual vocabulary ids.
"""
READS = ()

ITALIAN = set('''che di gli della delle dalla dalle dal nel nella nelle nei agli
allo alla dello degli quello quella quelli quelle questo questa questi queste
perché più anche quindi oppure cioè tuttavia molto sempre essere aveva hanno
viene stato sono siamo tutti tutte loro nostro nostra nostri oggi domani ieri
ciò già però né quale quali ogni senza quanto tutta tutto sul sulla sulle sui
negli dall dell nell sull'''.split())
ROMANCE = set('e la le si per con da non ma un una il lo del sul su tra fra cui'.split())
OTHER = set('''the and of to for is are this that with you he she it we they was
as on by an be has from have at which not but el los las que en y para es por
du des une et les dans der die das und ein eine ist von zu mit de do dos das
em um uma não com os ao pelo est sont pas pour sur avec vous nous aux ces ce
ne elle elles mais'''.split())
SPELLINGS = set('gli igli glia glio glie ggi aggi aggio iamo è ì ò ù'.split())

# Each row is a word class, a baseline, and an Italian-context increment.
WORD_CLASSES = [
    ('da dai', .19, 2.38),  # from
    ('dal dalla dalle dall dagli', .31, 1.19),  # from + article
    ('ai alle all agli allo', .02, 1.77),  # to + article
    ('a al alla ad', 0., .69),  # towards
    ('in con nel nella nelle nei negli nell', 0., .80),
    ('su sul sulla sulle sui sull tra fra', .04, 1.05),
    ('per', -.01, .64),  # for
    ('di della delle dell degli dello', -.13, .32),
    ('del', -.01, -.37),  # of + article
    ('il lo la le l', -.02, -.25),  # definite articles
    ('un uno una', -.05, -1.06),  # indefinite articles
    ('che', -.18, -.71),  # relative conjunction
    ('e o', .02, -.31),  # and/or
    ('ma non', .05, -.12),  # contrast/negation
    ('vi ti ci si', -.02, .42),  # personal pronouns
    ('chi cui gli', .21, 1.01),  # who/which, gli
    ('loro nostro nostra nostri nostre vostro vostra vostri', -.38, -.34),
    ('tutti tutte', .80, .29),  # all (quantifier)
    ('po', -.14, -1.16),  # po': a little
    ('ho ha hanno abbiamo sono siamo posso possono devo devono deve '
     'può era ero erano', 0., -.09),  # auxiliary/modal forms
    ('come anche quindi sempre perché perchè più dunque così', .02, .30),
    ('de', -.06, -.66),  # Romance of/from
    ('re', 0., -.84),  # Latin re- spelling
    ('es', .04, 1.78),  # Italian es- beginnings
]
WORDS = {w: (base, gain) for group, base, gain in WORD_CLASSES
         for w in group.split()}

# Productive prefixes and consonant-rich beginnings.
PREFIXES = [
    (('ri',), .01, 1.72),  # repetition, again
    (('rag', 'rac', 'rap'), .01, 1.16),  # assimilated ra-
    (('leg', 'colleg'), .05, 1.25),  # leg-/colleg- roots
    (('sp', 'sc', 'sf', 'sv', 'str'), 0., 1.04),
    (('cor', 'cost', 'comp', 'cond', 'col', 'contr'), 0., .58),
    (('ir', 'im', 'in'), 0., .45),  # in- and variants
    (('acq', 'acc', 'aff', 'ass', 'att', 'app', 'agg', 'amm',
      'avv', 'eff', 'off', 'imm', 'inn'), 0., 1.01),
]
VOWELS = 'aeiouàèéìòù'


# Inflectional endings and familiar syllable fragments, inside a word.
ENDING_CLASSES = [
    ('i', 0., .53),  # plural vowel
    ('o e', .01, -.38),
    ('ere re', -.07, -.71),  # infinitive endings
    ('are ire', .04, -.20),
    ('ore ale ano ico io ia za ze tà ità à è ò ù', -.01, -.32),
    ('ato ati ata ate uto uti uta ute ito iti ita ite', 0., .17),  # participles
    ('iamo ono ero', -.03, -.26),  # verb endings
    ('iv ivi ivo iva ist ista isti iste ic ici', .02, .63),  # adjectives
]
ENDINGS = {w: (base, gain) for group, base, gain in ENDING_CLASSES
           for w in group.split()}


def response(token, previous):
    word = token.strip().lower()
    beginning = bool(token) and token[0].isspace()
    if token == '</think>':
        return .24, 0.
    if not word:
        return 0., 0.
    if beginning:
        if word in WORDS:
            return WORDS[word]
        if word.startswith('qu'):
            return -.02, -.20  # question/demonstrative stems
    if not all('a' <= c <= 'z' or c in 'àèéìòù' for c in word):
        return -.003, 0.
    if word == 'gi':
        # Gemination split across tokens: rag + gi, mag + gi, etc.
        return .27 + .8 * previous.endswith('g'), 1.70
    if word in {'gli', 'igli', 'glia', 'glio', 'glie'}:
        return .33, 1.02
    if word in {'ggi', 'aggi', 'aggio', 'aggia', 'oggi'}:
        return .81, .24
    if word.startswith('gio'):
        return .28, .39
    if beginning:
        for starts, baseline, gain in PREFIXES:
            if word.startswith(starts):
                return baseline, gain
        return 0., .26 if word[-1] not in VOWELS else .07
    if len(word) <= 5 and any(p in word for p in ('tt', 'ss', 'nn', 'ff', 'pp')):
        return .04, 1.01
    if word.startswith('chi'):
        return .06, .71
    if word in ENDINGS:
        return ENDINGS[word]
    if word.endswith(('zione', 'zioni', 'enza', 'enze', 'ione', 'ioni')):
        return 0., -.23  # action nouns
    gain = .21 if word[-1] not in VOWELS else (.43 if word[-1] in 'iu' else -.03)
    return 0., gain


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        score, previous = -1., ''
    else:
        _, score, previous = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    if any(c.isalpha() for c in token):
        evidence = 0.
        if token and token[0].isspace():
            evidence += 2. * (word in ITALIAN)
            evidence += .4 * (word in ROMANCE)
            evidence -= 2. * (word in OTHER)
        if word.endswith(('zione', 'zioni')) or word in SPELLINGS:
            evidence += 3.
        score = max(-6., min(12., .985 * score + evidence))
    italian = max(0., min(1., score / 4.))
    baseline, gain = response(token, previous)
    return (doc, score, word), float(baseline + italian * gain)

"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:3135 -- a "written Italian" detector with a few word-level signs.

What it does, in plain terms:
- The component is mostly silent. It only speaks up inside Italian text.
- Italian-ness is estimated causally: within the current document, the share of
  Italian function words (di, che, il, sono, anche, ...) among all function words
  seen so far, against English ones (the, and, of, ...). Near 1 in Italian text,
  near 0 in English.
- Inside Italian text it is positive on Italian prepositions and article contractions
  (da, dal, dai, alle, gli, per, con, ...), negative on "che" and "un/una", and
  negative on short word-final pieces (-re, -ore, -ale, -ione, -o) that close a word.
Predicts (activation) = italian_score * sign_value(token).
"""
READS = ()

ITALIAN_FUNCTION = set("""di che il della delle degli gli nel nella sono anche questo questa come più
ma non tra fra sul dalla dal dai alle ai allo agli perché questi sia ci è sulla nei cui molto già
ancora stato stata una uno essere hanno""".split())
ENGLISH_FUNCTION = set("""the and of to in is that for with on as by it was are be this from at
or an which not have has""".split())
PREPOSITIONS = set("""per con da dal dai dalle dalla alle alla ai all al gli su sotto tra fra
nel nella nei sul sulla tutti chi oggi""".split())
WORD_FINAL = set("o re ere ore ale ione ono ano ico à ù ò è".split())


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: [Italian function words, English function words] seen in this document
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    if carry is None or prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        carry = [0, 0]
    token = tokens[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    if word in ITALIAN_FUNCTION:
        carry[0] += 1
    if word in ENGLISH_FUNCTION:
        carry[1] += 1
    italian = (carry[0] + 0.5) / (carry[0] + carry[1] + 1.0)

    core = token.strip()
    if not core.isalpha():
        sign = 0.0
    elif word in PREPOSITIONS:
        sign = 0.8
    elif word == "che":
        sign = -0.9
    elif word in ("un", "una"):
        sign = -0.5
    elif core in WORD_FINAL:
        sign = -0.45
    else:
        sign = 0.0
    return carry, italian * sign
